record.original_question: In the same adversarial contextual bandit setting with nested finite policy classes Π1 ⊂ Π2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ ΠM, can one design a model-selection algorithm that for every m ∈ [M] either (1) achieves regret Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K, M, log log |Π|) · √(T log |Πm|)), or (2) achieves regret Reg(Πm) ≤ O(poly(K, M, log log |Π|) · T^α log^(1−α) |Πm|) for some α ∈ [1/2, 1)? Alternatively, can one prove that no algorithm can achieve the second type of guarantee for any α ∈ [1/2, 1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the adversarial contextual bandit problem with $K$ actions and a finite policy class $\Pi$. At each round $t = 1, 2, \ldots, T$, an adversary chooses a context $x_t$ from a context space $\mathcal{X}$ together with a loss vector $\ell_t \in [0,1]^K$. The learner observes $x_t$, selects an action $a_t \in [K]$ (possibly using randomization), and observes only the bandit feedback $\ell_t(a_t)$. A policy is a map $\pi : \mathcal{X} \to [K]$. For a finite policy class $\Pi' \subseteq \Pi$, the regret to $\Pi'$ is
$$\mathrm{Reg}(\Pi') = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T} \ell_t(a_t)\right] - \min_{\pi \in \Pi'} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T} \ell_t(\pi(x_t))\right].$$

Suppose we are given a nested sequence of finite policy classes
$$\Pi_1 \subset \Pi_2 \subset \cdots \subset \Pi_M = \Pi.$$

Two questions are posed:

(A) Does there exist a single (model-selection) algorithm—not knowing in advance which class contains a good comparator—that, simultaneously for every $m \in [M]$, achieves
$$\mathrm{Reg}(\Pi_m) \;\le\; \mathrm{poly}(K, M, \log\log|\Pi|)\cdot \sqrt{T \log |\Pi_m|}?$$

(B) More weakly, does there exist a single algorithm and some constant $\alpha \in [1/2, 1)$ such that, simultaneously for every $m \in [M]$,
$$\mathrm{Reg}(\Pi_m) \;\le\; \mathrm{poly}(K, M, \log\log|\Pi|)\cdot T^{\alpha}\, (\log |\Pi_m|)^{1-\alpha}?$$

Either exhibit such an algorithm for (A) or (B), or prove that no algorithm can satisfy guarantee (B) for any value of $\alpha \in [1/2, 1)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the adversarial-setting variant of the Foster–Krishnamurthy–Luo COLT 2020 open problem on model selection in contextual bandits. Subsequent work (e.g., Pacchiano et al. 2020, Cutkosky et al. 2021 "Dynamic Balancing", Marinov–Zimmert 2021, "Best of Both Worlds Model Selection" 2022) provides partial progress and related upper/lower bounds, but no published result attains the desired poly(K,M,log log|Π|)·√(T log|Π_m|) or the T^α(log|Π_m|)^{1−α} guarantee for all m simultaneously in the adversarial setting, nor a matching impossibility result. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Model Selection for Contextual Bandits
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem statement on adversarial contextual bandits with nested finite policy classes asking for √(T log|Π_m|) or T^α log^{1-α}|Π_m| regret simultaneously, or an impossibility proof.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Best of Both Worlds Model Selection (2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies model selection in bandits with nested policy classes, providing high-probability stochastic and adversarial guarantees but not the form sought in the open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work gives partial progress without resolving the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Balancing for Model Selection in Bandits and RL
status_evidence.snippet: Provides model-selection algorithms with regret guarantees parameterized by base learner rates; results do not match the conjectured √(T log|Π_m|) form.
